content: # [BUG] A quality/gear effect's bonus for Tests silently stops applying **Describe the bug** An Active Effect that's supposed to add a bonus to a character for certain Tests no longer does anything. There's no error or warning anywhere — the effect is just quietly inert, and the roll dialog never reflects it. This particular effect is an older one: it was set up on this item a while ago, before a recent system update, and hasn't been touched since. Whatever fixes it needs to apply automatically wherever this shows up — however the old data happens to be stored, not just for this one example — without disturbing anything else already configured on the same effect or interfering with how the system brings other older content up to date. **Screenshots** The screenshot shows how this kind of effect is set up and what a correctly working one looks like — the pictured effect's own stored values aren't necessarily the exact data that needs fixing. **Versions (please complete the following information):** - FoundryVTT Version 13.351 - System Version 0.33.0

content.content:
200	Tests can be created with values from these sources:
201	- action
202	- test action defaults
203	- test action based on documents
204	
205	These different value providers will be merged in order of distance to the user by `TestCreator`, allowing a test implementation to take values from all of these sources and overwrite only those necessary. The closest user distance is given by the action, followed by the documents.
206	
207	### Class structure
208	Everything is based on the `SuccessTest` class, which defines general testing flow and also handles Foundry related interaction.
209	
210	The different Shadowrun 5 test types are created using subclasses:
211	- OpposedTest
212	- TeamworkTest
213	### Test flow
214	Triggering an active success test through an action will always show a dialog and chat message, both of which are optional.
215	
216	Should the action define a followup test, it will be initiated immediately for the active user.
217	
218	Opposing tests must be triggered manually by targeted actors through the chat message of the original active success test. Should the original action define a resist test, it will be initiated immediately for the opposing user.
219	
220	These behaviors are implemented within the `SuccessTest` and `OpposedTest` base classes and can be altered by implementing classes.
221	
222	### Actions and tests
223	Test implementations can be created fully without actions, though most players will trigger tests using any of the action items (action, weapon, spell, ...).
224	
225	Values from actions are taken to create configured test implementation. In general whenever a test defines default values (attributes, skill, modifiers, categories) these can be fully overwritten by what the action configures the test to use. If an action is given no configuration for any of a value, the default value of the test implementation will be used.
226	
227	### Tests and Active Effects
228	Active Effects can apply to tests, both in general and with a specific filter.
229	
230	#### Test implementations
231	Active Effects can target specific test implementations. In this case, the effect will only apply to actions using these tests.
232	
233	In general this should be used sparingly and is mostly a technical way of addressing tests. Instead, try using action categories. If you're missing an action category, inform us on our Discord channel on the FoundryVTT server or, better, the GitHub issues.
234	
235	#### Categories
236	Tests and actions can have categories. These are used to give tests a set of labels, allowing them to be targeted by an Active Effect.
237	
238	Typical use cases would be:
239	- matrix => a matrix action
240	- spell => any spell action
241	- social => any social skill action
242	- climbing => a climbing action
243	
244	Categories can be mixed and matched at will and don't have to adhere to sr5 rules.
245	
246	## Modifier implementation
247	The shadowrun5e system has multiple ways of handling modifiers on actors, items and 'situations':
248	- actor local modifiers
249	- situational modifiers
250	  
251	To define what modifiers a Shadowrun 5e Test uses an `action` can define a set of modifiers to use. These modifiers will be taken using the actors `ModifiersFlow` handler, sitting in between tests and modifiers applied onto a document.
252	### Actor local modifiers
253	The legacy modifiers are flat values for actors, which are taken as is and can be prepared during Document prepareData.
254	
255	Examples for these are modifiers for movement, armor and physical overflow.
256	### Situational modifiers
257	These modifiers depend upon the current situation a token / actor finds itself in at the moment. These can't be prepared beforehand but must be recalculated before values for each test can be used. They can be stored on all document types, but tend to be only on `Scene` and `SR5Actor` documents, which will be merged to a resulting situational modifier.
258	
259	This allows GMs to define broad situation modifiers for all actors on a specific scene, while also allowing to change some or all modifiers on an per actor basis as well.
260	
261	Examples for these are environmental, noise and recoil.
262	These modifiers can also be used to apply rules that need to recalculate between tests or combat turns or other changing events outside of an actors context or data preparation.
263	
264	## Actions
265	Any item can contain the action template allowing it to cast it as a Shadowrun 5e success test.
266

file.content:
Tests can be created with values from these sources:
- action
- test action defaults
- test action based on documents

These different value providers will be merged in order of distance to the user by `TestCreator`, allowing a test implementation to take values from all of these sources and overwrite only those necessary. The closest user distance is given by the action, followed by the documents.

### Class structure
Everything is based on the `SuccessTest` class, which defines general testing flow and also handles Foundry related interaction.

The different Shadowrun 5 test types are created using subclasses:
- OpposedTest
- TeamworkTest
### Test flow
Triggering an active success test through an action will always show a dialog and chat message, both of which are optional.

Should the action define a followup test, it will be initiated immediately for the active user.

Opposing tests must be triggered manually by targeted actors through the chat message of the original active success test. Should the original action define a resist test, it will be initiated immediately for the opposing user.

These behaviors are implemented within the `SuccessTest` and `OpposedTest` base classes and can be altered by implementing classes.

### Actions and tests
Test implementations can be created fully without actions, though most players will trigger tests using any of the action items (action, weapon, spell, ...).

Values from actions are taken to create configured test implementation. In general whenever a test defines default values (attributes, skill, modifiers, categories) these can be fully overwritten by what the action configures the test to use. If an action is given no configuration for any of a value, the default value of the test implementation will be used.

### Tests and Active Effects
Active Effects can apply to tests, both in general and with a specific filter.

#### Test implementations
Active Effects can target specific test implementations. In this case, the effect will only apply to actions using these tests.

In general this should be used sparingly and is mostly a technical way of addressing tests. Instead, try using action categories. If you're missing an action category, inform us on our Discord channel on the FoundryVTT server or, better, the GitHub issues.

#### Categories
Tests and actions can have categories. These are used to give tests a set of labels, allowing them to be targeted by an Active Effect.

Typical use cases would be:
- matrix => a matrix action
- spell => any spell action
- social => any social skill action
- climbing => a climbing action

Categories can be mixed and matched at will and don't have to adhere to sr5 rules.

## Modifier implementation
The shadowrun5e system has multiple ways of handling modifiers on actors, items and 'situations':
- actor local modifiers
- situational modifiers
  
To define what modifiers a Shadowrun 5e Test uses an `action` can define a set of modifiers to use. These modifiers will be taken using the actors `ModifiersFlow` handler, sitting in between tests and modifiers applied onto a document.
### Actor local modifiers
The legacy modifiers are flat values for actors, which are taken as is and can be prepared during Document prepareData.

Examples for these are modifiers for movement, armor and physical overflow.
### Situational modifiers
These modifiers depend upon the current situation a token / actor finds itself in at the moment. These can't be prepared beforehand but must be recalculated before values for each test can be used. They can be stored on all document types, but tend to be only on `Scene` and `SR5Actor` documents, which will be merged to a resulting situational modifier.

This allows GMs to define broad situation modifiers for all actors on a specific scene, while also allowing to change some or all modifiers on an per actor basis as well.

Examples for these are environmental, noise and recoil.
These modifiers can also be used to apply rules that need to recalculate between tests or combat turns or other changing events outside of an actors context or data preparation.

## Actions
Any item can contain the action template allowing it to cast it as a Shadowrun 5e success test.

All changes are in place (the new `Version0_33_1.ts` is untracked so not in the diff-stat, but it's registered and compiles).

## Summary

**Root cause.** The effect in the screenshot is an Apply-To **"Test"** effect. In the current system that value is `test_all` (the config maps `test_all` → label `SR5.Test` = "Test"), and `test_all` was split off from an earlier single `test` apply-to value (the other half being `test_item`). That split never shipped a migration.

So an older effect still stores `applyTo: 'test'`. Nothing matches it:
- `SuccessTestEffectsFlow.allApplicableEffects()` filters on `applyTo: ['test_all']` / `['test_item']`, so the effect is silently skipped — never reaching the roll dialog.
- The schema field (`ActiveEffectDM.applyTo`) has `choices: SR5.effectApplyTo`, so `'test'` is invalid and the `Sanitizer` quietly resets it to the `'actor'` default — no error, no warning. Exactly the "quietly inert" behavior reported.

(The `data.pool` change key is *not* broken — the flow rewrites `system.` → `data.` at apply time and both forms resolve to the test's pool, matching the working reference effect.)

**Fix.** Added `src/module/migrator/versions/Version0_33_1.ts`, a normal `VersionMigration` that converts `applyTo: 'test'` → `'test_all'` on active effects:
- `handlesActiveEffect` detects the legacy value in **either** `system.applyTo` or the pre-0.30.0 `flags.shadowrun5e.applyTo`, so it fires "however the old data happens to be stored."
- `migrateActiveEffect` only rewrites that one field, touching nothing else on the effect (changes, selections, etc. are preserved), and it slots into the existing ordered migrator chain, so it composes with the older migrations rather than interfering with them.
- Registered it in `Migrator.ts` (kept in ascending version order).
- Bumped `system.json` `version` to **0.33.1**. This is essential, not cosmetic: `Migrator.migrate` skips any document whose `_stats.systemVersion` equals `game.system.version`. Affected effects on worlds *already* on 0.33.0 get marked 0.33.0 (they carry a Custom change that the existing 0.33.0 migration touches), so without the bump the new migration would never run for them.

**Tests.** Added a `Version0_33_1` describe block in `Migrators.spec.ts` covering: `system.applyTo` conversion, flag-based conversion, that every other apply-to value (`actor`, `targeted_actor`, `test_all`, `test_item`, `modifier`) is left untouched, and that the rest of the effect config (selection tags, changes) survives.

`npx tsc --noEmit` passes; `eslint --quiet` reports 0 errors on all changed files (only the same `any`-usage warnings the entire migrator module already emits).

One thing I couldn't do here: the runtime quench tests need a live Foundry instance, so I validated via the type checker and linter rather than executing the new spec.
